label: Introduction
title: Introduction
html:
K.L.P. College is affiliated to IGU Meerpur Rewari, established in 1964, with an objective of imparting quality education to the aspiring students of South Haryana. Kishan Lal Public College has completed more than five decades in its pursuit of academic excellence. Under the aegis of Public Education Board Rewari, an independent governing body manages the college. Named after an educationist and a visionary philanthropist Late Pt. Kishan Lal Sharma, the college has earned a remarkable reputation in the state as a co-educational academic institute.


Late Smt. Javitri Devi (Wife of Late Pt. Kishan Lal Sharma) deserves special mention as the first donor towards the dream of an educational institute in the region. Her generous donation inspired others to come forward and collaborate to make this dream turn into a reality. Beginning its journey with just 250 students and a very limited infrastructure, the college now possesses a proud strength of approximately 3500 students and is successfully running various courses approved by Indira Gandhi University ,Meerpur ,Rewari .


The sustained efforts of the efficient governing bodies, hard working and committed faculty members and sincere students have made the college earn laurels in the field of not only academics but sports, social and other co-curricular activities as well. Established as an under graduate degree college initially, the college, in recent years has expanded far beyond its original limit. Its current profile of academic programmes of study includes not only the post-graduate degree courses but it offers a variety of professional and specialized courses also under self-finance scheme.


In recent years, the college has undergone a period of rapid infrastructural development. The new teaching blocks, fully air conditioned auditorium, the seminar rooms with audio-visual aids, the library with modification of infrastructure and availability of free internet facility, reflect new academic and enrolment growth. Various developments are ongoing to undertake significant projects of buildings and modernization in the coming years, spacious and well - designed cafeteria with aesthetic touch being the latest addition. The upgrading of classrooms and lecturing facilities, specialized science and computer labs, gymnasium ,indoor and outdoor sports, fully facilitated and digitalized libraries are some of the projects that mark the future not only of the college but also the students who join this college with an aim to become the dynamic learners capable of facing the challenges of life with knowledge, grit and determination.

label: History
title: History
html:
Excellence is not achieved in a day. Excellence has a preface. A preface, not less than a saga made of extraordinary events, real life heroes and a foundation ornamented with valour initiative scarifies and faith. A foundation so deep rooted and concrete which creates edified emitting values, knowledge, thoughts to the society at large and a character to its inhabitants. That excellence is what Kishan Lal Public College, has achieved in its fifty years of existence.

KLP College was established in 1964 by truly nationalists’ people in the revered memory of Sh. Kishan Lal Sharma, husband of Late Smt. Javitri Devi. The governing body of the college under Public Education Board, Rewari, has been running the institution on the path of progress with utmost dedication and enthusiasm. This college has the distinction of being one of the oldest colleges in Haryana. Today, college can boast of a special campus, state-of-art infrastructural facilities and highly acclaimed faculty trained at leading universities in India.

Though, the primary stress of the college is on achieving academic excellence, yet we also provide various opportunities to help students to enhance their knowledge and skills in the areas that we believe are important for their all round development. The College has always been at the forefront in educational innovations. As we celebrated our Golden Jubilee in 2014, we re calibrated ourselves to achieve higher distinctions and impart quality education. Notwithstanding its name, students from all religions have grown up here and excelled in the chosen areas of their interests, be it academic, sports and extracurricular activities.

The college provides a liberal, lively and competitive environment enabling students to carve out a niche for themselves in their chosen areas. Besides the infrastructural facilities, the strength of the college lies in its congenial and enriching atmosphere, which plays a crucial role in maintaining the excellent record the college is renowned for.

The college has seen remarkable growth over the years. Today, it is not only one of the most distinguished graduate & Post graduate co-educational institution in the country, but is also, by many accounts the college of first choice in surrounding area.

The college deserves the pride to have an exceptionally beautiful lush green campus, magnificent building of architectural beauty spreading over about 18 acres of land catering to overall development of more than 3000 students.

To keep pace with the exponential increase in students’ strength, the institution has augmented the infrastructure, providing enhanced parking area, ladies’ rooms (separate for students and staff) and canteen facilities, a spacious auditorium for conducting conferences, seminars, workshops etc. The college ensures optimum utilization of the infrastructure facilities provided. Well located and protected campus is the second paradise for the young boys and girls.

label: Principal’s desk
title: Principal’s desk
html:
I am delighted to welcome You to this college which is a unique and exciting educational community. We at Kishan Lal Public College, Rewari, believe that college life is not just a set of instructions or examinations but a series of experiences. Our attempt is to go beyond books, beyond instructions, beyond learning horizons. Having successfully crossed the various hurdles encountered on the way of its growth, the college has grown in stature and strength today, and has become one of the leading post graduate co-educational institutions of Haryana dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge and excellence.

In a world where everything is measured by the yardstick of success, we train our students to develop all round personality, positive attitude, self discipline, rational thinking and make up their mind to deal effectively with reality and ultimately transform into more creative, more productive and responsible citizens of the country. With immaculate academic ambience, state-of- art infrastructure, futuristic facilities and pronounced emphasis on quality education and overall development of the personality, the college has emerged as the top performing and leading college which offers a variety of duly approved courses of Indira Gandhi University, Meerpur (Rewari) across all professional,commercial and technical streams under the faculties of Commerce, Science, and Arts.

Besides the provision of almost all the popular subjects of B.A., B.Com., B.Com.(Hons) and B.Sc., the college is presently running Two Post Graduate programmes in , Geography and Commerce and also offer four professional courses in B.B.A., B.C.A., Bachelor course in Journalism & Mass Communication and B.Sc. in Biotechnology.

It is a matter of great satisfaction to my heart that the college is progressing by leaps and bounds in all fields. The college, all along its journey, has striven towards excellence with the collaboration of all the concerned, namely managements of the college, hard working faculty members, non-teaching staff, parents, students and well-wishers, to each one of whom we convey our sincere and profound appreciation with an ardent hope that they will ever continue to support and stand by the institution which they cherish so much.
I hope you will join us as a fellow-traveller on the path of self-discovery and capacity building.
My best wishes are with you for fulfilling your aspirations.

label: Facilities
title: Facilities
html:
The main strengths and features of the college are listed as under:

• Clean and pollution free campus spread over about 15.5 acres of land in the lush
green area.

• State-of-the-art facilities in all buildings.

• Well qualified and experienced faculty.

• Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) for maintaining academic standards and to improve quality of education.

• Well stocked Central library having a collection of a large number of reference books & text.

• Conduct of extension lectures, seminars, workshops and conferences, etc on regular basis.

• Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) as per new UGC guidelines combined with communication skills, personality development and value-based education.

• Regular Co-curricular activities for students. Facilitating scholarship Schemes for SC/ST, meritorious and economically backward students.

• Well-furnished seminars halls in all buildings with projector facilities.

• Internet facility and Wi-Fi enabled campus.

• A spacious and well-designed cafeteria with aesthetic touch. Variety of snacks and beverages are available.

• Gym for boys and girls.

• Regular industrial visits to provide practical exposure to students.

• Major enrolment of girl students of rural areas.

• Separate lawns for boys and girls.

• Centrally air-conditioned Auditorium and acoustically good with seating capacity of 700.

Library

The K.L.P Library system comprises of Kaladhari Gupta Pustakalaya and Self-finance Library that collectively support the teaching, research and extension programme of the College. The self-finance library houses a total collection of 26,710 books and 8 journals and some newspapers, All in-house operation facilities are available in the library. All syllabus books according to the course are provided to students of all semesters. All students, faculty and employees of the colleges are entitled for the membership of the library.

The college has a separate library for career oriented courses. The library has 67,226 number of text books and reference books, magazines and 6 journals for the students for ready reference.

Canteen

The canteen is primarily responsible for serving nutritious and hygienic food to the students and staff. It also serves meals to the students residing in the campus.

Computer Labs

The college proudly possesses nine spacious, wellmaintained and fully equipped computer labs to cater to different needs arising out of different curricula. These labs are well updated and have state-of-the-art hardware and software infrastructure. All the labs have high speed internet connectivity. Students have access to these labs as per their requirements.

Auditorium

The college has a state-of-the-art 'Prem Lata Jain Auditorium'. The auditorium has a marvellous interior and exterior. The fully air conditioned auditorium has a capacity of 700 persons.

The auditorium is being intensely used for college activities and has become the hub of academic and co-curricular activities.

(ख) पिछड़ी-जाति के विद्यार्थियों के लिए छात्रवृत्तियाँ :-

जो विद्यार्थी पिछड़ी जाति छात्रवृति प्राप्त करना चाहता है, एडमीशन फार्म के साथ ही निम्नलिखित प्रमाण-पत्रो के साथ ही महाविद्यालय कार्यालय में जमा करा दें । ये प्रमाण-पत्र है :

html:
फीस माफी एवं आर्थिक सहायता के नियम

कॉलेज में फीस माफ कराने एवं आर्थिक सहायता प्रदान करने के निम्नलिखित नियम होंगे :-।

1. किशनलाल पब्लिक कॉलेज कं प्राध्यापकों एवं कर्मचारियों के वार्ड को छोड़कर किसी भी विद्यार्थी कौ प्रवेश के समय फीस माफ नहीं की जाएगी ।

2. फीस माफी एवं आर्थिक सहायता प्राप्त करने के लिए आवेदन करना होगा ।

3. इसके लिए प्राचार्य एक Fee Concession Commitee नियुक्त करेंगे । इस समिति कौ सिफारिश पर हो किसी छात्र/छात्रा की फीस माफ की जाएगी/आर्थिक सहायता प्रदान की जाएगी ।

4. फीस माफ करते समय विद्यार्थियों की आर्थिक स्थिति, शैक्षिक योग्यता व अनुशासन के साथ उच्च स्तर के खेल व अन्य गतिविधियों में भाग लेने आदि का विशेष ध्यान रखा जाएगा ।

5. यदि दो भाई/बहन इस कॉलेज में पढ़ते है तो छोटा भाई आधी फीस माफ प्रवेश के समय या फीस माफी के समय कर लें । इसके पश्चात्‌ फौस माफ नहीं की जाएगी ।

सुरक्षा निधि

कॉलेज से सुरक्षा निधि प्राप्त करने के लिए आवश्यक होगा कि कॉलेज द्वारा निर्धारित आवेदन पत्र पर अंकित सभी जानकारी एवं घर का स्थायी पता स्पष्ट रूप से दें । इसमें किसी प्रकार की कमी होने पर आबेदन-पत्र स्वीकार नहीं किया जायेगा । आवेदन-पत्र आगामी सत्र के 3। अगस्त तक स्वीकार किये जायेंगे । सुरक्षा निधि मनीआर्डर/चैक द्वारा सत्र के अंत तक अर्थात्‌ 3। मार्च तक भेज दी जाएगी ।

नोट :- विद्यार्थी को चाहिए कि थे फीस /जुर्माना/अन्य सभी प्रकार की नकद राशि College Counters पर ही जमा कराएँ । पैसा जमा कराने के पश्चात्‌ रसीद अवश्य प्राप्त कर ले, अन्यथा राशि जमा नहीं मानी जाएगी । ना

NSS

There are three active units of NSS in the college through which the spirit of nationalism is instilled in students. Apart from this, under the aegis of these units, various programs of social, cultural and community welfare are organised like Blood donation camps, tree plantations, literacy etc. Regular One day and Seven Day camps are organised to conduct these activities. Students who are a part of NSS are given various benefits regarding their admissions and jobs in various organisations. We encourage all the students to register for NSS.

NCC

To instil the values of discipline, national defence and social work, NCC units are established in various institutions of the country. 8 Haryana Battalion of NCC is active in our college and students can apply their registration through NCC of the college. Students are trained in various fields under NCC like mountaineering, leadership, national integration programs, Republic Day parade camps and several other national camps. The students who obtain NCC C or B certificate are given special advantage to join Indian Armed Forces and other job opportunities. For more information, students can get in touch with the NCC officer.

title: Student code of conduct
html:
Conduct And Discilpline Rules

1.Applicaion of Rules

These rules shall apply to all the students of IGU Meerpur.

2 Acts of Indiscipline and Misconduct.

. Any act of misconduct committed by a student inside or outside the campus shall be an act of violation of discipline of the University. Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, violation of the discipline shall

• Disruption of teaching, study, examination, research or administrative work, curricular or extra curricular activity or residential life of the members of the University, including any attempt to prevent any member of the University or its staff from carrying on his or her work and doing any act reasonably likely to cause such disruption.

•Damaging or defacing University property or the property of the members of the University or any other property inside or outside the University Campus.

• Engaging in any attempt as wrongful confinement of teachers, officers, employees and students of the University or camping inside or creating nuisance inside the boundaries of houses of teachers, officers and other members of the University.

• Use of abusive and derogatory slogans or intimidatory language or incitement of hatred and violence or any act calculated to further the same.

• Smoking in the University Campus.

• Eve-teasing or disrespectful behaviour to women or girl students.

• Any assault upon or intimidation of or insulting behaviour towards a teacher, officer, employee or student or any other person.

• Causing or colluding in the unauthorised entry of any person in the campus or in the unauthorised occupation of any portion of University premises, including Hostels or Halls of Residence, by any person.

• Getting enrolled in more than one course of study simultaneously in violation of University rules.

• Committing forgery, tampering with or misuse of University documents or records, identification cards etc..

• Furnishing false certificate or false information to any office under the control and jurisdiction of the University.

• Consuming or possessing alcoholic drinks, dangerous drugs or other intoxicants in the University premises.

• Indulging in acts of gambling in the University premises.

• Possessing or using weapons such as knives, lathis, iron chains, iron rods, sticks, explosives and fire arms in the University premises.

• Arousing communal, caste or regional feelings or creating disharmony among students.

•• Not disclosing one’s identity when asked to do so by an employee or officer of the University who is authorized to ask for identity.

• Tearing of pages, defacing, burning or destroying books of any library or seminar.

• Unauthorized occupation of Hostel Rooms or unauthorised use of University furniture in one’s Hostel Room or elsewhere.

.Accommodating guests or other persons in Hostel without permission of the competent authority.

.• Improper rendering of accounts for money drawn from or through any office under the control and jurisdiction of the University.

.• Coercing the medical staff to render medical assistance to persons not entitled for the same or any other disorderly behaviour.

.• Any act of moral turpitude.

.• Any offence under law.

.•• Committing any of the offences specified in the examination (Control of unfair means and disorderly conduct) of the University

.• Violation of Traffic Rules as notified by the Proctor.

.•• Pasting of posters or distributing pamphlets, handbills etc. of objectionable nature or writing on walls and disfiguring building.

.•• Any other act which may be considered by the Vice-Chancellor or the Discipline Committee to be an act of violation of discipline.

3 Disciplinary Action.

Without any prejudice to the powers of the Vice-Chancellor as specified under Statute 39, the following Officers are authorized to take disciplinary action by way of imposing penalties as specified in Clause 4 of these regulations other than those specified in Sub-Clause (ix), (x), (xi), (xii), (xiii) & (xiv):

• Proctor • Deans of the Faculties/Dean, Students Welfare. • Provost • Heads of the Departments • Principals of the Colleges/Institutions •

Any other person employed by the University and authorised by the Vice-Chancellor for the purpose provided that the penalties on the offences relating to Examinations will be dealt with by the relevant bodies.

4. Nature of Penalties :

The following penalties may, for acts of indiscipline or misconduct or for good and sufficient reasons, be imposed on a student, namely:

• Written warning and information to the guardian. • Fine as may be warranted by the nature of case. • Suspension from the Class/Department/College/Hostel/Mess/Library or withdrawal of any other facility of this nature. • Suspension or cancellation of scholarships, fellowships or any financial assistance from any source, or recommendation to that effect to the sanctioning agency. • Recovery of pecuniary loss caused to University property. • Debarring from participation in Sports/NCC/NSS and other such activities. • Disqualifying from holding any representative position in the Class/ College/ Hostel/ Mess/Sports/Clubs and in similar other bodies. • Hostel shift and Hall shift. • Expulsion from the Department/Faculty/Hostel.Mess/Library/Clubs for a specified period. • Debarring from an examination. • Non-issue of Migration Certificate. • Expulsion from the University for a specified period. • Disqualifying from further studies, or prohibition for future admission or re-admission. • Any student against whom an allegation of misconduct has been made may be suspended from the rolls of the University by the Vice-Chancellor, pending enquiry or pending trial on a cognizable offence by a court of Law. 5.Opportunity to be Given before Award of Penalty

No penalty, provided in sub-clauses (ix), (x), (xi), (xii), (xiii) and (xiv) of Clause 4 shall be imposed without giving to the student a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

6. Review of/Appeal against the Penalty

A review would lie to the Officer issuing the orders within seven days, and an appeal would lie against the orders of the authorities mentioned in these rules (except the Vice-Chancellor) to the Proctorial Board. The Board may also review its decision at its own.

7. Prohibition of Ragging The instruction for curbing ragging as conveyed by the UGC vide letter No. FA-I/ 97 (CPP-II) dated 7th July, 2001 in view of the judgement of Supreme Court in Civil Writ Petition No. 656 of 1998 ‘VishwaJagriti Mission V/s Centre Govt.’ given below shall be adhered to strictly :

Ragging in educational institutions is banned and any one indulging in ragging is likely to be punished appropriately, which punishment may include expulsion from the Institute, suspension from the institution or classes for a limited period or fine with a public apology. The punishment may also take the shape of (i) withholding scholarships or other benefits (ii) debarring from representation in events (iii) withholding results (iv) suspension or expulsion from hostel or mess, and the like.(v) lodging of FIR to local police. If the individuals committing or abetting ragging are not/ cannot be identified, collective punishment can be awarded to act as a deterrent.

Any disorderly conduct whether by words spoken or written or by an act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness to any other student, indulging in rowdy or indiscipline activities which cause or is likely to cause annoyance, hardship or psychological harm or to raise fear or apprehension thereof in freshers or junior students or asking the students to do any act or perform something which such students

will not do in the ordinary course and which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of shame or embarrassment, so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of a fresher or a junior student will be deemed to be an act of ragging.

Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in SLP(C) No. 24295/2004 in the matter of University of Kerala V/s Council of Principals, Colleges of Kerala and others has ordered that if any incident of ragging comes to the notice of the authority, the concerned student shall be given liberty to explain, and if his explanation is not found satisfactory, the authority would expel him from the Institution.

The applicants at the time of admission are required to give an affidavit (Appendix O) against ragging. 8. Check on the menace of sexual harassment and violence against females

Sexual harassment is taken as a serious act of indiscipline. A Committee, constituted by the Vice-Chancellor under the Chairmanship of Prof. Mrs. Sunita Malhotra, Dept. of Psychology, will check the menace of sexual harassment and violence against females. The “Sexual Harassment” includes any unwelcome sexually determined behaviour, whether directly or by implication and includes physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually-coloured remarks, showing pornography or any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature. The Committee shall take all precautionary measures to prevent sexual harassment and violence against female students in the University. It shall also ensure that there is no hostile environment towards females. No female student should have reasonable ground to believe that she is at a disadvantage or is being discriminated against. If any complaint of sexual harassment comes to the notice of the Committee, immediate disciplinary action along with appropriate action in accordance with the law would be taken.

-Principal K.L.P COLLEGE rewari

NCC is a responsive, learning and continuously evolving organization. It encourages cadets to have a sense of patriotic commitment, to contribute to national development, respect for diversities in religion, language, culture, ethnicity, lifestyle and habitat. The NCC provides opportunities to the youth of the country for their all-round development with a sense of Duty, Commitment, Dedication, Discipline and Moral Values so that they become able leaders and useful citizens. K.L.P College NCC wing is among the best in University.The N.C.C provides exposure to the cadets in a wide range of activities, with a distinct emphasis on Social Services, Discipline and Adventure Training. The NCC is open to all regular students of the college on a voluntary basis. The students have no liability for active military service.


N.C.C. Report 2021-22

एन.सी.सी ऑफिसर लेफ्टिनेट संजय कुमार के नेतृत्व में वर्तमान सत्र की शुरुआत केएलपी कॉलेज के 54 कैडेट्स में अपना पंजीकरण करवाकर की। कॉलेज के एन.सी.सी कैडेट्स व एन.सी.सी ऑफिसर ने विभिन्न पाँव गतिविधियों में भाग लेकर कॉलेज के साथ साथ हरियाणा राज्य का नाम रोशन किया। दिनांक 26 जुलाई 2021 को के एल.पी कॉलेज एन. सी. सी यूनिट द्वारा कारगिल विजय दिवस मनाया गया। कार्यक्रम के चीफ गेस्ट 8 हरियाणा बटालियन रेवाड़ी के कमांडिंग अफसर कर्नल संजय राजन एवं गेस्ट ऑफ ऑनर एक एमफलर कर्जल सुरेंद्र सिंह यादव ने भारत के रणबांकुरों ने पाकिस्तान को जो करारी मात दी थी, उस इतिहास को याद किया। कार्यक्रम में केएलपी कॉलेज में पौधारोपण किया गया। इस दौरान विशिष्ट अतिथि 8 हरियाणा बटालियन के कर्नल संजय राजन व अन्य सैन्य अधिकारी मौजूद रहे। केएलपी कॉलेज से लेफ्टिनेट संजय शर्मा तथा कॉलेज के प्रिसिपल डॉ अभय सिंह ने कैडेट्स को स्वच्छ भारत स्वस्थ भारत और कारगिल सुदूध में शहीद हुए सैनिकों के अदम्य साहस के बारे में बताया और अमर शहीदों को याद किया गया। इसी दौरान कैडेट्स में रेजांगला युद्ध स्मारक पर साफ सफाई की


दिनांक 21 दिसंबर 2021 से 27 दिसंबर 2021 तक केएलपी कॉलेज के एन.सी.सी कैडेट ने गवर्नमेंट पॉलिटेक्निक लिसाना में आयोजित एनुअल ट्रेनिंग डे कैडर कैंप में भाग लिया। 26 जनवरी 2022 को गणतंत्र दिवस पर राव तुलाराम स्टेडियम रेवाड़ी में जिला स्तरीय परेड में अंडर ऑफिसर नितिन राठी के नेतृत्व में कॉलेज के 30 कैडेट्स ने भाग लिया। दिनांक 08/02/ 2022 को के. एल. पी. कॉलेज के परिसर में एन.सी.सी यूनिट के कैडेट्स के द्वारा बाय काट सिंगल यूज प्लास्टिक विषय पर पोस्ट स्लोगन बनाए गए तथा रैली निकाली गई प्रोग्राम में के. एस पी कॉलेज के एन.सी.सी कैडेट्स ने हिस्सा लिया तथा कॉलेज स्टूडेंट्स को संदेश दिया कि हमें अपने जीवन में प्लास्टिक का इस्तेमाल नहीं करना चाहिए प्लास्टिक हमारे पर्यावरण के लिए हानिकारक है। इसके साथ रैली के माध्यम से समाज तथा आसपास के लोगों को भी यह संदेश पहुंचाया। कार्यक्रम में केएलपी कॉलेज के प्रिंसिपल डॉ अभय सिंह यादव, एन. सी. सी ऑफिसर लेफ्टिनेंट संजय कुमार पी आई हवलदार विजय शंकर यादव उपस्थित रहे। दिनांक 27 फरवरी 2022 को के एस.पी कॉलेज के एन. सी. सी कैडेट्स ने चंदशेखर आजाद के बलिदान दिवस पर कॉलेज प्रांगण में उनकी शहादत की याद किया तथा श्रद्धा सुमन अर्पित किए। कॉलेज के एम. सी सी अफसर लेफ्टिनेट संजय कुमार में कैडेट्स को बताया की स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में पद्रशेखर आजाद की शहादत को भुलाया नहीं जा सकता। चंद्रशेखर आजाद आजाद थे और हमेशा आजाद ही रहे। वर्तमान सत्र के अंत में बी सर्टिफिकेट के लिए 18 कैडेट्स ने एग्जाम दिया तथा सी सर्टिफिकेट के लिए 16 कैडेट्स ने एक्जाम दिया।

A WARM WELCOME TO OUR VIEWERS ABOUT NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME (NSS)

National Service Scheme, popularly known as NSS, was formally launched on 24th September, 1969, during the Gandhi Centenary Year as it was Gandhi Ji who inspired the Indian Youth to participate in the movement for Indian independence and the social uplift of the down-trodden section of society. National Service Scheme is a student centered programme and it is complementary to education. It is a noble experiment in academic extension. It inculcates the spirit of voluntary work among students and teachers through sustained community interaction. It brings our academic institutions closer to the society. It is a link between the campus and community, the college and village, knowledge and action. The overall aim of NSS is the Personality Development of students through community service. It gives an extension dimension to Higher Education system and orients the student youth to community service.

The National Service Scheme (NSS) is a Central Sector Scheme of Government of India, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. It provides opportunity to the student youth of 11th & 12th Class of schools at +2 Board level and student youth of Technical Institution, Graduate & Post Graduate at colleges and University level of India to take part in various government led community service activities & programmes. A student enrolled as NSS volunteer will have to put in 120 hours for community work in a year for a period of 2 years. He/she is likely to participate in different programmes and projects under NSS. NSS volunteer, who has completed 240 / 360 hours of regular activities in the period of P.G. student for 2 years / Degree student for 3 years and attended two 7 Days special camps, will be issued an NSS certificate by the respective university.

The sole aim of the NSS is to provide hands on experience to young students in delivering community service. In 1969, Union Education Minister Dr. V. K. R. V. Rao, launched the NSS programmed in 37 Universities covering all States. Since inception of the NSS in the year 1969, the number of students strength increased from 40,000 to over 3.8 million up to the end of March 2018 students in various universities, colleges and Institutions of higher learning have volunteered to take part in various community service programmes.


NSS BADGE

The NSS symbol is embossed on the NSS badge. The NSS volunteers wear it while undertaking any programme of community service.

• The Konark wheel in the symbol has eight bars which represent the 24 hours of the day.
• The Red colour in the badge indicates that the NSS volunteers are full of blood. I.e. lively, active energetic and full of high spirit.
• The Navy Blue colour indicates the cosmos of which the NSS is a tiny part, ready to contribute its share for the welfare of mankind.

NSS LOGO

The symbol of the NSS is based on the ‘Rath’ wheel of the Konark Sun Temple situated in Orissa. These giant wheels of the Sun Temple portray the cycle of creation, preservation and release, and signify the movement in life across time and space.

YRC Activities

The Indian Red Cross Society (IRCS) was established under the provision of section 2 of the IRCS Act XV of 1920 with its national Head Quarters in New Delhi. The core focus of IRCS is to promote humanitarian principles and values, disaster management, healthcare in community and blood services. The Youth Red Cross is the most important constituent of its mother organization, Indian Red Cross Society. It is a group movement organized at the initial stages for students between 18 and 25 years of age. We, in our college, have a Youth Red Cross wing. Any student of any discipline can become a YRC member. Under the guidance of Programme Officer, the students are trained and encouraged to manage various programmes. The motto of YRC is “to serve”.



Principles of YRC:
1. Humanity 2. Impartiality 3. Neutrality 4. Independence 5. Voluntary Service 6. Unity 7. Universality

Objectives of YRC:

1. To conduct social and health awareness progrmmes.
2. Awareness on the care of their own health and that of others.
3. To encourage the students to extend their humanitarian services to the society.
4. To offer First Aid Training to the YRC volunteers.
5. To develop leadership qualities among the students.
6. The understanding and acceptance of civic responsibilities and acting according to the humanitarian concern to fulfill the same.
7. National integration.
8. To foster better friendly relationship with all without any discrimination

Youth Red Cross Unit members are the builders of the nation who take part in bringing the very Motto of Red Cross that is “SERVICE TO SOCIETY”.

html:
Red Ribbon Club

Introduction:

RRC is a voluntary on campus programme implemented by government in higher educational institutions to prompt voluntary blood donation, to aware the youth about various social evils mainly HIV-AIDS, Drug addiction, Drunk and driving. Red Ribbon is an international symbol of HIV/AIDS awareness since 1991.It got popularity in the year of 1992. The New York Times declared 1992 as "The year of Ribbon." At that time, President Clinton set up the White House Office of National AIDS Policy to create awareness among the citizens. Now a day’s red ribbon had gotten so much attention for HIV- AIDS. The objective of Red Ribbon Club is to create awareness among students about STD/HIV/AIDS and let them spread this awareness among the society. It is the movement started by our government in the school and colleges to aware the youth regarding the disease which still has no cure. It can only prevented not cured. As Prevention is better than cure and prevention can only be done by creating awareness among the society about this disease. The red ribbon club organizes awareness camps at regular time intervals to support the persons suffering from HIV-AIDS and to aware the students. So that the youth can prevent themselves, their neighbourhood, friends and society by spreading the right knowledge about AIDS. Red is symbol of warning about the biggest non curable disease of our time. Red also represent the blood, anger, love, passion and the pain of the persons suffering from HIV-AIDS. RRC also encourages the students for blood donation and inculcate the feeling to serve the society.


Objectives: The specific objectives of the RRC are as under • To motivate youth and build their capacity as peer educators and inculcate the skills of leadership, negotiation and team work among students. • To promote voluntary blood donation among youth and increase access to safe and adequate quantities of blood. • As youth are nation builders, let them feel the responsibility of change mediator and prevent the society from social evils by creating awareness among their neighbourhood and society. • To reduce the new HIV infection among youth by providing them the proper knowledge of Sex, Sexuality, Drugs and their side effects and HIV-AIDS. • To inculcate the spirit of providing help and support to the persons living with HIV. • To aware the youth about the causes and prevention of HIV-AIDS.

RRC IN K.L.P. College

K.L.P. College Rewari has an active unit of red ribbon club, which works for the students and with the students to create awareness among them and society. RRC organises various awareness programme in collaboration with YRC and NSS.



RRC Team:
Mrs Pushpa Yadav (RRC Incharge) Mrs Monika Yadav Dr Sangeeta

List of various activities organised:

• T.B. awareness program was organized in association with civil hospital Rewari in seminar hall of our college. Mrs Seema Ansari (District program coordinator) and Mrs Vinita (DPPMC) had shared their valuable information regarding T.B. with students and emphasized to give their contribution to society to eliminate TB till 2025, as our government targets. Students were encouraged to spread this knowledge among their Neighbourhood, family and friends.



An Essay writing competition” was organized in college. Topics were given on the spot, to inculcate originality of thoughts among the students. 15 students have taken part in this competition. Topics given were: 1. Raising legal age of marriage for women 2. Hijab controversy in India 3. Role of students in eradication of drugs 4. Addiction of social media 5. Degradation of moral values among youngsters



• A medical camp (to check haemoglobin) for female students was organized in association with YRC wing of college and Indian medical association Rewari on 5th May 2022 in college library. 250 girls had given their samples to check out their haemoglobin. On the same day a valuable lecture was delivered by Dr Suman Yadav on the topic Anaemia, Causes and its prevention. Program was graced by the presence of Dr Krishna Kumar (CMO Rewari), IMA President Dr R. B. Yadav, Dr Abhay Singh Yadav (Principal) RRC and YRC incharges and their team members



• An awareness program on HIV /AIDS, prevention control and treatment was organized in seminar hall. This program was organized by Red Ribbon Club and Youth Red Cross of KLP College Rewari in association with Haryana state legal service authority and health department Rewari. Mrs Varsha Jain (CJM Rewari) was the chief guest and had given her valuable suggestions and information to the students about legal activities and HIV /AIDS. Doctor Chetna , Mrs Suman Yadav (counsellor) and Sh Harish Kumar had also shared their knowledge about HIV/ AIDS with our students

WOMEN CELL,KLP COLLEGE, REWARI

Women cell plays an important role in voicing opinions on important matters that affect the daily life of women students. It provides a platform where students can comfortably participate and share their views. It also train women to acquire wide range of skills and knowledge, to develop and increase their social, economic and intellectual capacities for peace, security and prosperity of mankind. The Women Cell of Klp college started with the aim of empowering and orienting women to recognise their true value, potential and to help them attain their own stand in a competing world. It’s aim is the overall development of women in all spheres of their life. It helps in creating awareness among women on a range of issues from empowerment to environment.


Objectives
  • 1 To help students to change their mindset and attitude towards life in terms of women.
  • 2 To create awareness, instill values and develop the personality and leadership quality.
  • 3 To impart knowledge on legal rights of women.
  • 4 To organize workshops on personality development.
  • 5 To enhance self-esteem and self confidence among women students and staff.
  • 6 To foster decision making ability.
  • 7 To build a positive image of women in the society and recognise their contributions in every sphere
  • 8 To conduct guest lecturers by eminent people from different fields.

Members of cell
1 Dr. Pratibha (Convenor) 2 Mrs. Sangita (Geog.) 3 Dr. Mamta Sharma 4 Dr. Jyotsna 5 Dr. Monika Kumari 6 Dr. Divya

The Women Cell of the college organised a talk on Sustainable Ways to Manage Periods: All about Menstrual Cups by Dr Archana Yadav, Obstretician and Gynaecologist. She delved in detail in her talk about the harmful impact of Mentrual Waste on the environment and the huge landfills it is causing to the earth year after year and how switching to Menstrual Cups is so imperative to female health, hygiene as well as the environment. She demonstrated in detail the types and sizes of cups and how to use them according to individual needs. In a small town like Rewari, this information and knowledge was path breaking because of lack of general sensitivity and awareness towards women issues and environment. It was a successful program as lot of students and staff members asked their doubts and questions and were given satisfactory response by the speaker. Students also pledged to try to switch to cups from sanitary towels


The convenor of the Women Cell and Organising Secretary of this talk Dr.Pratibha urged the female students to ask questions and get better of their doubts regarding Menstrual Cups. The students were forthcoming in asking their various queries and Dr Pratibha directed them to the speaker, at the end of the talk all the staff members and students pledged to take this small step towards sustainability and female hygiene by switching to Menstrual Cups.

label: Environmental club
title: Environmental club
html:
The objective of college environmental club is to promote environmental awareness among students. It aims to sensitize students on different environmental issues such as global warming,pollution ,deforestation ,exploitation of natural resources etc. It is a forum that empowers students to participate and take up meaningful environmental activities and projects.

Development of a Mini Forest on the college ground through Miyawaki Technique. Objectives of the Practice -To restore a potential degraded land patch of the college rapidly and effectively by forestation. -To create a natural carbon sink and encourage biodiversity. -To promote greener environment and help reduce pollution, attract birds and insects. -To make the stakeholders aware of Miyawaki technique for rapid forestation. Context Earth is losing its forest cover rapidly. Deforestation is responsible for global carbon emissions, soil erosion and bio-diversity loss. So, when a local NGO Bharat Vikas Parishad approached the college for collaboration to develop a Mini Forest, because of the ample availability of the potential land of our college ground - the idea was welcomed enthusiastically. The Practice The work to develop the land patch into a mini forest started around the beginning of the year 2021 when Bharat Vikas Parishad got the nod of the college authorities to work on this very unique project. In this method propounded by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, the forest grows rapidly by the construction of soil, utilizing native plant diversity, growing healthy saplings and planting them close together. .

The first step was to choose the potential natural vegetation, then saplings were grown in bags full of organic manure, then planting site was prepared with organic bio- mass and saplings were finally planted densely-three to four per square meter. The saplings compete with each other for sun light to grow rapidly. Only native species that would occur naturally in that area without humans, given the specific climatic condition, are planted. It is really heartening to see diverse variety of useful plants like cherry, orange, tamarind, sweet lime, pomegranate, blackberries, laburnum, drumsticks, neem, sacred fig, night jasmine(also known as harsingaar and parijaat) etc. growing into beautiful trees with care and regular monitoring by the NGO, authorities and the extremely efficient gardeners of the college. Evidence of Success The institution boasts of a mini dense forest of its own after approx. a year and half from the commencement of this project. It is a great learning for all the stakeholders specially students that it is so easy to develop a mini forest with natural and organic methods and no big investments. A great haven for the great number of bio-diversity already present in the college, this forest is a unique feature of our institution and a remarkable example before the local communities and other institutions, a step towards reducing carbon footprint and a great contribution towards a cleaner, greener environment

To build and ensure a quality culture aimed at all round excellence at the institutional level


Mission

To channelize and systematize the efforts and measures of an institution towards academic excellence.
To be the driving force for ushering in quality to remove deficiencies and enhance quality


Role

To develop quality systems for conscious, consistent and catalytic programmed action to improve the academic and administrative performance of the College. To promote measures for institutional functioning towards quality enhancement through internationalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best practices

title: Campus at a glance
html:
• The Library:

The K.L.P Library system comprises of Kaladhari Gupta Pustakalaya and Self-finance Library that collectively support the teaching, research and extension programme of the College. The self-finance library houses a total collection of 26,710 books and 8 journals and some newspapers, All in-house operation facilities are available in the library. All syllabus books according to the course are provided to students of all semesters. All students, faculty and employees of the colleges are entitled for the membership of the library.
The college has a separate library for career oriented courses. The library has 67,226 number of text books and reference books, magazines and 6 journals for the students for ready reference. A sizeable amount is regularly allocated and utilized for the purchase of new editions of books recommended by the members of faculty. In addition to this, the library has subscribed newspapers and periodicals for the students of professional courses for their information update. The students are encouraged to utilize library facility to the maximum. A separate library for PG. classes has been established to facilitate students, research scholars and faculty members to meet all their educational needs.





• Cafeteria



• INTERNET FACILITY :

Library provides free internet access to all the students and faculty members.

• DELNET:

The K.L.P College is a member of DELNET. As such, the users from College can access databases hosted by DELNET.

• N LIST :

The K.L.P College is a member of N-LIST, entitled National Library and Information Services Infrastructure for Scholarly Content (N-LIST). It provides access to various e-resources to students.

• Seminar Rooms :

For an effective teaching set up, the college has two seminar rooms with audio-visual teaching aids. The rooms have sufficient space to accommodate a large number of students.

• Computer Labs:

The college proudly possesses nine spacious, wellmaintained and fully equipped computer labs to cater to different needs arising out of different curricula. These labs are well updated and have state-of-the-art hardware and software infrastructure. All the labs have high speed internet connectivity. Students have access to these labs as per their requirements.

• Auditorium:

The college has a state-of-the-art 'Prem Lata Jain Auditorium'. The auditorium has a marvellous interior and exterior. The fully air conditioned auditorium has a capacity of 700 persons.
The auditorium is being intensely used for college activities and has become the hub of academic and co-curricular activities.

Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)

|

• IQAC is a significant administrative body responsible for all quality matters. It is the prime responsibility of IQAC to initiate, plan and supervise various activities which are necessary to increase the quality of the education imparted in college. It has to submit AQAR online to NAAC.

• Vocational Training
As a part of curriculum, the students of B.B.A. are required to prepare a report on the in-plant training in the third year of course. The training provides the students to have first hand experience of the industrial/organizational environment related to any particular aspect. The students, under the supervision of the faculty members, prepare this report. The report is a part of evaluation for B.B.A. course. The college has identified a good number of organizations/industries around Rewari town and nearby where our students regularly go for in-plant training programmes.

• Counseling and Placement Cell
Keeping in view the career oriented courses, the college has an established Counselling and Placement Cell. To explore the opportunities of placement, concrete efforts are made by the Placement Cell to assist the students in being suitably placed in industrial houses of repute. A large number of organizations, public and private have shown considerable interest in students and have provided training facility and placement to them. Our cell equips the students with the requisite communication skills in the fields, which enables them to take the challenges of the corporate world with the confidence borne out of competence.

• Mentoring:
The institute has an active 'mentoring system' through which a group of ten to fifteen students is assigned to one faculty member, who looks after the all round developmental needs of students. The endeavour is to develop and promote stressfree mutual healthy relationship between the guide and the learner to have greater self-reliance and enhance the learning process. These sessions between the tutor and the students address personal and social problems of students along with those involving studies and career guidance. They are guided how to handle peer pressure, manage time effectively, overcome performance anxiety and drug-abuse, alcoholism etc. These interactive sessions significantly enhance intellectual, introspective and problem solving abilities of our students.

• Extension Lectures & other Academic Programmes:
In every semester, extension lectures are arranged for the students from time to time. Renowned and expert academicians, industrialists and other specialized intellectuals are invited to groom the students on various topics. Industrial visits are also an important part of the B.B.A. , B.Com(Hons.), M.Com. and B.Sc. (Biotech) programmes. These visits provide the students exposure to multiple dimensions of industry including nature of work, labour requirements, managerial practices, sales and marketing, use of human resources and new technologies etc. The college has given emphasis on monitoring the placement opportunities for the professional students.
